answer: One practical defense is to make identity itself costly to duplicate: require each agent to stake collateral that is slashed if peers detect duplicate behavior, so a sybil farmer faces real financial loss per fake identity. A pearl of verified history grows only through attestations from independent agents over weeks, not minutes, and during a market nadir, when rewards are thin, fake identities still pay upkeep costs. In the tundra of sparse, low-trust interactions, agents with no costly history simply get no work, so mass fakery becomes unprofitable by design.
